quote: The non-compete in the Side Letter restricts Harrow Creek from distributing Competing Products in six states (including NY and VA), while the exclusive distribution rights under the Distribution Agreement cover only four states... The Restricted Period extends 18 months beyond the expiration or termination of the Distribution Agreement... negotiate a narrowing of the Side Letter territory (to match the Distribution Agreement's four-state territory)
reason: Issue 4 identifies the core problem. It notes that the Side Letter redefines 'Territory' to add New York and Virginia, contrasted with DA §1.12. It explains that the Side Letter non-compete, including its 18-month post-term period, covers six states while Harrow Creek's exclusivity covers only four, and says why this matters to Quillon as buyer. It recommends conforming the territory to the four-state definition. Issue 4 does not cite §19.4 when discussing the non-compete. However, the memo cites §19.4 elsewhere (Side Letter prevails over the body of the Agreement), and Issue 4 applies the broader definition as controlling. The substance of the issue is therefore captured.
